questions.stem: Why are most stomata found on the lower surface of a leaf rather than the upper surface?

options.text: Because the upper surface needs to be waterproof to collect rainwater
Because the lower surface receives more light for photosynthesis
Because carbon dioxide is heavier than air and sinks to the bottom of the leaf
Because having stomata on the shaded lower surface reduces water loss from evaporation

questions.explanation: The lower surface of a leaf is shaded from direct sunlight, so it is cooler. Having stomata mainly on this surface reduces the rate of evaporation of water from the leaf, helping to minimise water loss while still allowing gas exchange.
